statesNote: Monthly premium for a 40-year-old, KFF State Health Facts 'Average Marketplace Premiums by Metal Tier', timeframe 2026. bronze40 = Average Lowest-Cost Bronze Premium; silver40 = Average Benchmark Premium (second-lowest-cost silver). KFF method: lowest-cost (or benchmark) premium for a 40-year-old in each county, weighted by county plan selections; may include non-EHB premium. These are unsubsidized, averaged statewide - an estimate only; county-level prices vary widely.

ageCurve._notes: Source: CMS 'State Specific Age Curve Variations' (5-31-2017, effective PY2018), still the latest curve file linked from CMS's Market Rating Reforms page (page table updated 12/10/2021, page modified 09/10/2024). Band '64' = 64 and older. Federal default is used by every state not listed here. MA is published on its own base (age 21 = 1.183, max ratio 2:1) and is NOT normalized to age 21 = 1.000; divide by 1.183 if the tool needs a 21-based ratio. MN differs from the federal default only for ages 0-20 (0.890). AL's curve applies to the individual market only (CMS column header 'Alabama (Individual)'). NJ has a small-group-only curve in the same file and is omitted here; NJ individual market follows the federal default per the CMS table. NY and VT are community rated (1:1 age ratio) so no curve applies.

familyTiers._note: CMS State Specific Family Tier Ratios table (Market Rating Reforms page; table updated 12/10/2021). Multiply the single-adult rate by the tier factor. Not re-verified against NY DFS / VT DFR 2026 filings.

fpl2025._note: 2025 HHS poverty guidelines (FR Doc. 2025-01377, published 1/17/2025), used for 2026-coverage PTC eligibility. Household size n: base + (n-1)*perPerson (the published tables are exactly linear, e.g. contiguous 4 = $32,150, 8 = $54,150). 400% FPL single contiguous = $62,600.

applicablePctNote: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-25 section 3.01. Bands are 'at least lower but less than upper' except the last, which is 'at least 300% but not more than 400%'. Percentage rises linearly within each band. No credit above 400% FPL. PTC eligibility generally starts at 100% FPL (below that, Medicaid or, in non-expansion states, the coverage gap). Required contribution percentage (employer affordability) 2026 = 9.96%.
subsidyStatusNote: The ARPA/IRA enhanced premium tax credits expired on December 31, 2025, so the original ACA schedule above applies for 2026 and the 400% FPL cliff is back. December 2025: Senate votes on competing extension bills (incl. S. 3385) failed to reach 60 votes. January 8, 2026: House passed H.R. 1834, a three-year clean extension, 230-196; the Senate has not passed it and no extension has been enacted. A bipartisan Senate compromise (CARE Act, 2-year extension with minimum premiums/income caps) was reported in Jan 2026 but not enacted. Peterson-KFF (July 8, 2026, updated Aug 3, 2026) still describes the credits as expired and the 400% cliff as in effect. No source found showing any enactment through late September 2026. Some state-based marketplaces (e.g. NM) partly back-filled with state subsidies; the federal calculation does not include those.

moop2026._note: Final PY2026 maximum annual limitation on cost sharing per the Marketplace Integrity and Affordability final rule (90 FR 27074, June 25, 2025), which replaced the $10,150/$20,300 figures first published in the 2026 Payment Notice. PY2025 was $9,200/$18,400.

bronze.avgDeductibleNote: KFF, Cost-Sharing for Plans Offered in the Federal Marketplace for 2026 (Nov 5, 2025): average medical deductible in bronze plans with a combined medical+drug deductible, HealthCare.gov states, 2026 (88% of bronze plans have a combined deductible). Plan average, not enrollment-weighted. Cross-check: our own plan-level average from the CMS PY2026 landscape file = $7,502 for combined-deductible bronze plans (median $7,500).
bronze.avgMoopNote: NOT a KFF figure - KFF's 2026 deck gives out-of-pocket limits only for silver. Computed by us from the CMS PY2026 HealthCare.gov landscape file (individual_market_medical, 30 HealthCare.gov states): unweighted mean individual in-network MOOP across 1,300 unique bronze + expanded bronze plans = $9,950; median $10,000; most common values $10,000 (442 plans), $10,600 (356), $10,150 (198). Excludes state-based-marketplace states.
bronze.pcpNote: From the same CMS PY2026 landscape file (1,300 unique bronze/expanded-bronze plans, HealthCare.gov states, unweighted): 68.9% have a flat primary-care copay that is NOT subject to the deductible, 6.5% cover PCP visits at no charge before the deductible, 0.7% have a pre-deductible copay plus coinsurance, and 23.9% apply the deductible first (no charge / copay / coinsurance after deductible). So ~76% of HealthCare.gov bronze plans give some pre-deductible PCP coverage. Among pre-deductible copays: median $50, mean $50.8, most common $50 (571 plans). CMS's 2026 standardized expanded-bronze design also sets a $50 pre-deductible PCP copay. Some plans limit pre-deductible visits (e.g. first 3 visits) - the landscape file does not show visit caps. State-based marketplaces (e.g. Covered California's first-3-visits design) are not included.
bronze.genericRxNote: CMS PY2026 landscape file, same 1,300 bronze plans: 75.0% charge a flat generic copay not subject to the deductible, 2.5% cover generics at no charge pre-deductible, 22.5% apply the deductible first. Pre-deductible generic copays: median $25, mean $20.4, most common $25 (502 plans), then $3 (164) and $30 (96). HealthCare.gov standardized plans are required to cover generics pre-deductible with a fixed copay.
bronze.bronzeShareOfEnrollees2026: 40% of plan selections (9.2M) in 2026, up from 30% (7.3M) in 2025 - KFF, May 19, 2026.

nonExpansionNote: KFF Status of State Medicaid Expansion Decisions, as of August 2026: 41 states incl. DC adopted, 10 not. Georgia runs a limited 'Pathways' program with work requirements and Wisconsin covers adults to 100% FPL without formal expansion, but both are listed by KFF as Not Adopted. In non-expansion states, adults under 100% FPL generally fall in the coverage gap (no PTC).
gaps: states: none - all 50 states + DC filled for 2026 from KFF (both bronze and benchmark are 2026).

bronze.avgMoop: no KFF/CMS published national bronze average found; value is our own unweighted computation from the CMS PY2026 HealthCare.gov landscape file (30 states only, excludes state-based marketplaces).

bronze PCP and generic Rx figures: our computation from the same CMS landscape file (HealthCare.gov states only, plan-level not enrollment-weighted); no KFF/Peterson national 2026 bronze PCP/generic analysis found. Visit caps on pre-deductible copays are not captured.
bronze.avgDeductible: KFF figure is for HealthCare.gov states only and is a plan average, not enrollment weighted.

ageCurve: CMS's newest published state curve file is for PY2018 (5-31-2017); state curve changes after that are not captured by CMS and were not individually re-verified with state insurance departments. MA curve is not normalized to age 21 = 1.000 (see ageCurve._notes). NJ small-group-only curve omitted.
familyTiers NY/VT: from CMS table dated 12/10/2021; not re-verified against 2026 state filings.
subsidy status: latest source confirming no extension is Peterson-KFF updated Aug 3, 2026; nothing later than that found either way.
